st_augustine.name: Waves Lawn Program v13 (St. Augustine)
notes: Waves lawn program v13: one program for every grass. Product limits stay as product-pick warnings.
One whole-lawn tool per visit: hose (110-gal skid tank and reel) or spreader, plus backpack spots.
No N or P from June 1 through September 30 (North Port: April 1). Reclaimed-water lawns (purple pipes or caps): the tech logs half the N at every N visit; the app does not adjust it yet.

No pre-emergent on sod in its first growing season or on thin or recovering turf. A pre-emergent needs 0.5 in of rain or irrigation within 14 days (Stonewall: label; Dimension: owner rule 2026-10-09); the customer's regular watering counts.
Fungicide, insecticide and post-emergent products are spot work only. The one exception is May Tetrino on sunny turf.

Never use the same chemical group twice in a row. Two exceptions: Group 3 pre-emergents (all of them are Group 3 this season; owner accepted 2026-10-06) and the take-all pair (Artavia, then Headway 30 days later, or Artavia twice; both recorded for take-all).

Large patch: Artavia, then Velista. Prevent on mapped areas in October and November when the soil falls through 80 F, at 2 gal per 1,000 sq ft. A lawn mapped for both take-all and large patch already had Artavia in September and Headway in October (both Group 11), and the Headway label allows no more than 2 consecutive Group 11 (QoI) applications: its October large patch pass is Velista alone and its December curative is Velista. A lawn mapped for large patch only keeps Artavia, then Velista. Velista (Group 7) works on large patch, not take-all; azoxystrobin does nothing on dollar spot.
Gray leaf spot: Artavia, then Gravex.
Take-all: Artavia first, then Headway 30 days later, on mapped areas, in spring and again in fall. No curative once the roots are black.

Artavia then Headway is the planned take-all pair: Headway adds propiconazole (group 3) to the same azoxystrobin (group 11), so group 11 repeats once and this is the named take-all exception below. Headway take-all rate: 3 fl oz per 1,000 sq ft, 30 days after the Artavia pass on every grass (the Headway liquid label, EPA 100-1216, limits bermudagrass to 3 fl oz per 1,000 sq ft every 30 days, so the pair uses 30 days on all three tracks).

Chinch bugs: always count before treating. Push a bottomless can 3 in into the soil at 4 spots on the edge of the damage, fill with water, count for 5 minutes, and write the count in the visit notes. Big-eyed bugs (wide head, bulging eyes) are predators: do not count them. Recheck a treated area at 5 and 12 days. Where chinch bugs are found at the edge of a damaged patch (4 gal per 1,000 sq ft into the thatch): Tetrino in May, then Arena, then bifenthrin, then Dylox 6.2 G. Arena: 0.147 oz per 1,000 sq ft (6.4 oz per acre, the low end of the label's turf range; about 1.4 level teaspoons), up to 2 applications per lawn per year at least 8 weeks (56 days) apart (app-enforced). Two applications reach the label's yearly limit of 12.8 oz per acre (0.4 lb clothianidin per acre); after that, use bifenthrin, which is not a neonicotinoid. On St. Augustine this rate and the 8-week repeat are Valent's Florida 2(ee) recommendation for southern chinch bug (EPA Reg. No. 59639-152; expires December 31, 2028): keep a copy on the truck. Keep Arena off blooming plants where bees forage, and keep children and pets off until the spray has dried.

Sugarcane mosaic virus (lethal viral necrosis) is confirmed in Sarasota, Manatee and Charlotte. Yellow streaks between the veins on Floratam or ProVista, in any month (most often September to January), with no chinch bugs: photo, note and call the office; Waves sends live streaked leaves with their roots to the UF Plant Diagnostic Center at its own cost (roots too, because take-all can come with the virus). Do not sell a fungicide or insecticide for it (UF: pesticides do not work). Mow or walk suspect lawns last. For new sod, recommend Palmetto or CitraBlue, never Floratam or ProVista.
Caterpillars: Acelepryn, then bifenthrin, with a 7-day recheck. Acelepryn on caterpillars: delay watering (irrigation) or mowing for 24 hours after application.
Bifenthrin: delay watering 24 hours on every use. Grubs and mole crickets: Dylox 6.2 G on spreader visits only, watered in.

Mole cricket nymphs, June and the July scout visit (UF/IFAS and Clemson: treat small nymphs from mid-June through July, before they grow): Advion Insect Granule (indoxacarb, Group 22A) on the tunnel areas, 3 lb per 1,000 sq ft of treated area by hand shaker. It is a bait and a spot tool, not a whole-lawn tool, so the one-tool rule holds. If the soil is dry, water the spot lightly BEFORE applying. Apply late in the day to dry grass. Then no irrigation and no rain-dependent watering for 3 days. On the June hose visit, the bait goes on after the micronutrient pass has dried. Label yearly maximum: 4.6 lb per 1,000 sq ft, so Advion goes on a spot once a year, at 3 lb. The July visit is for new tunnel areas that were not baited in June. Fall adults and bigger mole crickets go to Dylox 6.2 G. Acelepryn is not a mole cricket product in this program.

Weeds: Celsius plus Certainty (0.085 oz plus 0.028 oz per 1,000 sq ft, NIS 0.25%); once the Celsius annual cap is reached, Blindside Herbicide in its place from November through March (April through October: no weed spray once the Celsius cap is reached). In February the weed spot is Celsius alone: no Certainty and no surfactant. Blindside goes on at 0.149 oz per 1,000 sq ft, one application per lawn per year (label: the warm-season rate is 0.149 to 0.23 oz a pass, and no more than 0.23 oz per 1,000 sq ft (10 oz per acre) a year). Dismiss: use up the jug on green kyllinga under 85°F, no rain or irrigation for 24 hours after (owner 2026-10-09: every post-emergent herbicide holds 24 hours); do not reorder.
Dry spots: Dispatch Sprayable.

Other spot diseases (secondary lines): Pythium root rot with Artavia in June, July and August (September's Artavia is the take-all pass only, so a take-all application stays unambiguous); fairy ring with Velista and a wetting agent; dollar spot on bermuda and zoysia with Velista or Gravex, never Artavia (its label says it does not control dollar spot); rust on zoysia with Velista or Gravex; leaf spot or melting out on bermuda with Velista. The app warns on the second Artavia application for Pythium; the label allows two in a row. Headway is not a rotation for it (Headway has the same Group 11 ingredient). Do not make a third Group 11 application in a row: fix the watering or drainage.

Fire ant granule (Topchoice Granular Insecticide) is an optional add-on in April or October, both spreader visits, one application per lawn per year. The office prices it. It is not part of the base visit.
Ronstar / oxadiazon: never on residential home lawns (label: not for use on home lawns); commercial turf per label.

Soil tests: triggers only (owner 2026-10-31). Take a sample only when one of these is true: a new sod or new-build lawn is not thriving 60 days after install; yellowing stays after the iron spot test, or the lawn is no better after 2 visits with no pest or disease found (October to May only); it is a bahia or pasture-origin lawn; or phosphorus is planned in Manatee County. One sample per lawn, once (two only when a problem spot differs from the rest of the lawn); never retest. Pull 10 to 15 cores from the top 4 in, mix them, and bag 1 pint; never mix healthy and problem turf, and never sample right after a fertilizer or lime pass. The office mails it to the UF/IFAS Extension Soil Testing Laboratory (standard test, form SL136) and records the test date and pH in the turf profile. Act on three results only: lime at the report's lime rate; magnesium (Epsom salt, rate set by the office) when Mg is below 20 ppm; phosphorus only when P is 20 mg/kg or lower (Mehlich-3) and the report is filed with Manatee County. Any other result changes nothing. A soil test comes before a UF plant lab sample, never both at once. Lab reports are not sent to customers unless the owner says so.

Plant-parasitic nematodes: when a lawn keeps thinning, with short, stubby roots and no chinch bugs, and its soil test (above) found nothing to act on, the office sends one soil-and-root sample to the UF/IFAS Nematode Assay Lab at Waves' own cost, taken the way the lab's turf form says. One sample per lawn, once. Nothing is sold for nematodes (UF/IFAS: home lawns have no reliable nematode control). Lab reports are not sent to customers unless the owner says so.

Fertilizer safety: deflector shield on the spreader, a 10 ft fertilizer-free band from any water body, wetland, seawall or top of bank, no fertilizing when a severe thunderstorm, flood or tropical watch or warning is forecast, sweep fertilizer off driveways, sidewalks and streets back onto the lawn, Manatee BMP decal on the vehicle.

North Port: no Nutra-TECH on the June, August and September visits until the city confirms. The April Nutra-TECH pass stays. The plan holds the summer product back and a completion that records it is flagged.

Season 2027 (visits from 2027-10-01), 12-visit plan only. This is a note and changes no 2026 visit: October LESCO 24-0-11 with PolyPlus OPTI at 2.5 lb per 1,000 sq ft (0.60 lb N); November LESCO Dimension 0.21% 18-0-10 at 4.04 lb per 1,000 sq ft (0.73 lb N, 0.37 lb dithiopyr per acre, the commercial label Coastal South rate). January Stonewall 4FL stays. December is defined separately. The 9-visit plan keeps the October Dimension step.
safety_rules: Celsius WG: stay under the annual cap (Celsius and Certainty: up to 2 applications per lawn per year each; Blindside: 1 application per lawn per year); use Blindside after the Celsius cap, November through March only (April through October: no weed spray once the Celsius cap is reached), at 0.149 oz per 1,000 sq ft, one application per lawn per year (label: warm-season rate 0.149 to 0.23 oz a pass, no more than 0.23 oz per 1,000 sq ft a year). Spray in the morning. Celsius + Certainty and Blindside: no rain or irrigation for 24 hours after (owner 2026-10-09: every post-emergent herbicide holds 24 hours). No mowing 2 days before or after. In summer, only on watered turf.
Tetrino: sunny turf only, at least 25 ft from water, applied alone.
Bifenthrin (Atticus Talak 7.9 F): delay watering 24 hours.

Dylox 6.2 G: spreader visits only, water in. For grubs, mole crickets and chinch bugs only, 3 lb per 1,000 sq ft. At most 2 applications per lawn per calendar year, at least 7 days apart (Waves rule; the label allows 3). Not for sod webworms, armyworms or cutworms under this program: the label's yearly amount for those surface feeders is lower (261 lb of product per acre).

Advion Insect Granule (mole cricket bait, indoxacarb, label EPA Reg. No. 100-1483): spot bait on tunnel areas only, 3 lb per 1,000 sq ft of treated area by hand shaker, never through an irrigation system. Soil dry: water the spot lightly before. Apply late in the day to dry grass. No irrigation or rain-dependent watering for 3 days after (rain or irrigation within 2 to 3 days can cut control). Sweep granules off hard surfaces. A spot is baited once a year, at 3 lb; label yearly maximum 4.6 lb per 1,000 sq ft.
Dismiss: use up the jug on green kyllinga under 85°F, no rain or irrigation for 24 hours after (owner 2026-10-09: every post-emergent herbicide holds 24 hours); do not reorder.
Pre-emergent: no pre-emergent on first-year sod or thin or recovering turf; it needs 0.5 in of rain or irrigation within 14 days (Stonewall: label; Dimension: owner rule 2026-10-09).
N and P blackout Jun 1 - Sep 30 (North Port Apr 1); the tech logs half the N on reclaimed-water lawns (the app does not adjust it yet).

Do not repeat a chemical group on the next application. Exceptions: Group 3 pre-emergents (all of them are Group 3 this season; owner accepted 2026-10-06) and the take-all pair (Artavia, then Headway or Artavia), both recorded for take-all.

Fertilizer safety: deflector shield on the spreader, a 10 ft fertilizer-free band from any water body, wetland, seawall or top of bank, no fertilizing when a severe thunderstorm, flood or tropical watch or warning is forecast, sweep fertilizer off driveways, sidewalks and streets back onto the lawn, Manatee BMP decal on the vehicle.
North Port: no Nutra-TECH June through September until the city confirms.
Ronstar / oxadiazon: never on residential home lawns (label: not for use on home lawns); commercial turf per label.

notes: Waves lawn program v13: one program for every grass. Product limits stay as product-pick warnings.
One whole-lawn tool per visit: hose (110-gal skid tank and reel) or spreader, plus backpack spots.
No N or P from June 1 through September 30 (North Port: April 1). Reclaimed-water lawns (purple pipes or caps): the tech logs half the N at every N visit; the app does not adjust it yet.

No pre-emergent on sod in its first growing season or on thin or recovering turf. A pre-emergent needs 0.5 in of rain or irrigation within 14 days (Stonewall: label; Dimension: owner rule 2026-10-09); the customer's regular watering counts.
Fungicide, insecticide and post-emergent products are spot work only. The one exception is May Tetrino on sunny turf.

Never use the same chemical group twice in a row. Two exceptions: Group 3 pre-emergents (all of them are Group 3 this season; owner accepted 2026-10-06) and the take-all pair (Artavia, then Headway 30 days later, or Artavia twice; both recorded for take-all).

Large patch: Artavia, then Velista. Prevent on mapped areas in October and November when the soil falls through 80 F, at 2 gal per 1,000 sq ft. A lawn mapped for both take-all and large patch already had Artavia in September and Headway in October (both Group 11), and the Headway label allows no more than 2 consecutive Group 11 (QoI) applications: its October large patch pass is Velista alone and its December curative is Velista. A lawn mapped for large patch only keeps Artavia, then Velista. Velista (Group 7) works on large patch, not take-all; azoxystrobin does nothing on dollar spot.
Gray leaf spot: Artavia, then Gravex.
Take-all: Artavia first, then Headway 30 days later, on mapped areas, in spring and again in fall. No curative once the roots are black.

Artavia then Headway is the planned take-all pair: Headway adds propiconazole (group 3) to the same azoxystrobin (group 11), so group 11 repeats once and this is the named take-all exception below. Headway take-all rate: 3 fl oz per 1,000 sq ft, 30 days after the Artavia pass on every grass (the Headway liquid label, EPA 100-1216, limits bermudagrass to 3 fl oz per 1,000 sq ft every 30 days, so the pair uses 30 days on all three tracks).

Chinch bugs: always count before treating. Push a bottomless can 3 in into the soil at 4 spots on the edge of the damage, fill with water, count for 5 minutes, and write the count in the visit notes. Big-eyed bugs (wide head, bulging eyes) are predators: do not count them. Recheck a treated area at 5 and 12 days. Where chinch bugs are found at the edge of a damaged patch (4 gal per 1,000 sq ft into the thatch): Tetrino in May, then Arena, then bifenthrin, then Dylox 6.2 G. Arena: 0.147 oz per 1,000 sq ft (6.4 oz per acre, the low end of the label's turf range; about 1.4 level teaspoons), up to 2 applications per lawn per year at least 8 weeks (56 days) apart (app-enforced). Two applications reach the label's yearly limit of 12.8 oz per acre (0.4 lb clothianidin per acre); after that, use bifenthrin, which is not a neonicotinoid. On St. Augustine this rate and the 8-week repeat are Valent's Florida 2(ee) recommendation for southern chinch bug (EPA Reg. No. 59639-152; expires December 31, 2028): keep a copy on the truck. Keep Arena off blooming plants where bees forage, and keep children and pets off until the spray has dried.

Sugarcane mosaic virus (lethal viral necrosis) is confirmed in Sarasota, Manatee and Charlotte. Yellow streaks between the veins on Floratam or ProVista, in any month (most often September to January), with no chinch bugs: photo, note and call the office; Waves sends live streaked leaves with their roots to the UF Plant Diagnostic Center at its own cost (roots too, because take-all can come with the virus). Do not sell a fungicide or insecticide for it (UF: pesticides do not work). Mow or walk suspect lawns last. For new sod, recommend Palmetto or CitraBlue, never Floratam or ProVista.
Caterpillars: Acelepryn, then bifenthrin, with a 7-day recheck. Acelepryn on caterpillars: delay watering (irrigation) or mowing for 24 hours after application.
Bifenthrin: delay watering 24 hours on every use. Grubs and mole crickets: Dylox 6.2 G on spreader visits only, watered in.

Mole cricket nymphs, June and the July scout visit (UF/IFAS and Clemson: treat small nymphs from mid-June through July, before they grow): Advion Insect Granule (indoxacarb, Group 22A) on the tunnel areas, 3 lb per 1,000 sq ft of treated area by hand shaker. It is a bait and a spot tool, not a whole-lawn tool, so the one-tool rule holds. If the soil is dry, water the spot lightly BEFORE applying. Apply late in the day to dry grass. Then no irrigation and no rain-dependent watering for 3 days. On the June hose visit, the bait goes on after the micronutrient pass has dried. Label yearly maximum: 4.6 lb per 1,000 sq ft, so Advion goes on a spot once a year, at 3 lb. The July visit is for new tunnel areas that were not baited in June. Fall adults and bigger mole crickets go to Dylox 6.2 G. Acelepryn is not a mole cricket product in this program.

Weeds: Celsius plus Certainty (0.085 oz plus 0.028 oz per 1,000 sq ft, NIS 0.25%); once the Celsius annual cap is reached, Blindside Herbicide in its place from November through March (April through October: no weed spray once the Celsius cap is reached). In February the weed spot is Celsius alone: no Certainty and no surfactant. Blindside goes on at 0.149 oz per 1,000 sq ft, one application per lawn per year (label: the warm-season rate is 0.149 to 0.23 oz a pass, and no more than 0.23 oz per 1,000 sq ft (10 oz per acre) a year). Dismiss: use up the jug on green kyllinga under 85°F, no rain or irrigation for 24 hours after (owner 2026-10-09: every post-emergent herbicide holds 24 hours); do not reorder.
Dry spots: Dispatch Sprayable.

Other spot diseases (secondary lines): Pythium root rot with Artavia in June, July and August (September's Artavia is the take-all pass only, so a take-all application stays unambiguous); fairy ring with Velista and a wetting agent; dollar spot on bermuda and zoysia with Velista or Gravex, never Artavia (its label says it does not control dollar spot); rust on zoysia with Velista or Gravex; leaf spot or melting out on bermuda with Velista. The app warns on the second Artavia application for Pythium; the label allows two in a row. Headway is not a rotation for it (Headway has the same Group 11 ingredient). Do not make a third Group 11 application in a row: fix the watering or drainage.

Fire ant granule (Topchoice Granular Insecticide) is an optional add-on in April or October, both spreader visits, one application per lawn per year. The office prices it. It is not part of the base visit.
Ronstar / oxadiazon: never on residential home lawns (label: not for use on home lawns); commercial turf per label.

Soil tests: triggers only (owner 2026-10-31). Take a sample only when one of these is true: a new sod or new-build lawn is not thriving 60 days after install; yellowing stays after the iron spot test, or the lawn is no better after 2 visits with no pest or disease found (October to May only); it is a bahia or pasture-origin lawn; or phosphorus is planned in Manatee County. One sample per lawn, once (two only when a problem spot differs from the rest of the lawn); never retest. Pull 10 to 15 cores from the top 4 in, mix them, and bag 1 pint; never mix healthy and problem turf, and never sample right after a fertilizer or lime pass. The office mails it to the UF/IFAS Extension Soil Testing Laboratory (standard test, form SL136) and records the test date and pH in the turf profile. Act on three results only: lime at the report's lime rate; magnesium (Epsom salt, rate set by the office) when Mg is below 20 ppm; phosphorus only when P is 20 mg/kg or lower (Mehlich-3) and the report is filed with Manatee County. Any other result changes nothing. A soil test comes before a UF plant lab sample, never both at once. Lab reports are not sent to customers unless the owner says so.

Plant-parasitic nematodes: when a lawn keeps thinning, with short, stubby roots and no chinch bugs, and its soil test (above) found nothing to act on, the office sends one soil-and-root sample to the UF/IFAS Nematode Assay Lab at Waves' own cost, taken the way the lab's turf form says. One sample per lawn, once. Nothing is sold for nematodes (UF/IFAS: home lawns have no reliable nematode control). Lab reports are not sent to customers unless the owner says so.

Fertilizer safety: deflector shield on the spreader, a 10 ft fertilizer-free band from any water body, wetland, seawall or top of bank, no fertilizing when a severe thunderstorm, flood or tropical watch or warning is forecast, sweep fertilizer off driveways, sidewalks and streets back onto the lawn, Manatee BMP decal on the vehicle.

North Port: no Nutra-TECH on the June, August and September visits until the city confirms. The April Nutra-TECH pass stays. The plan holds the summer product back and a completion that records it is flagged.

Season 2027 (visits from 2027-10-01), 12-visit plan only. This is a note and changes no 2026 visit: October LESCO 24-0-11 with PolyPlus OPTI at 2.5 lb per 1,000 sq ft (0.60 lb N); November LESCO Dimension 0.21% 18-0-10 at 4.04 lb per 1,000 sq ft (0.73 lb N, 0.37 lb dithiopyr per acre, the commercial label Coastal South rate). January Stonewall 4FL stays. December is defined separately. The 9-visit plan keeps the October Dimension step.

notes: Waves lawn program v13: one program for every grass. Product limits stay as product-pick warnings.
One whole-lawn tool per visit: hose (110-gal skid tank and reel) or spreader, plus backpack spots.
No N or P from June 1 through September 30 (North Port: April 1). Reclaimed-water lawns (purple pipes or caps): the tech logs half the N at every N visit; the app does not adjust it yet.

No pre-emergent on sod in its first growing season or on thin or recovering turf. A pre-emergent needs 0.5 in of rain or irrigation within 14 days (Stonewall: label; Dimension: owner rule 2026-10-09); the customer's regular watering counts.
Fungicide, insecticide and post-emergent products are spot work only. The one exception is May Tetrino on sunny turf.

Never use the same chemical group twice in a row. Two exceptions: Group 3 pre-emergents (all of them are Group 3 this season; owner accepted 2026-10-06) and the take-all pair (Artavia, then Headway 30 days later, or Artavia twice; both recorded for take-all).

Large patch: Artavia, then Velista. Prevent on mapped areas in October and November when the soil falls through 80 F, at 2 gal per 1,000 sq ft. A lawn mapped for both take-all and large patch already had Artavia in September and Headway in October (both Group 11), and the Headway label allows no more than 2 consecutive Group 11 (QoI) applications: its October large patch pass is Velista alone and its December curative is Velista. A lawn mapped for large patch only keeps Artavia, then Velista. Velista (Group 7) works on large patch, not take-all; azoxystrobin does nothing on dollar spot.
Gray leaf spot: Artavia, then Gravex.
Take-all: Artavia first, then Headway 30 days later, on mapped areas, in spring and again in fall. No curative once the roots are black.

Artavia then Headway is the planned take-all pair: Headway adds propiconazole (group 3) to the same azoxystrobin (group 11), so group 11 repeats once and this is the named take-all exception below. Headway take-all rate: 3 fl oz per 1,000 sq ft, 30 days after the Artavia pass on every grass (the Headway liquid label, EPA 100-1216, limits bermudagrass to 3 fl oz per 1,000 sq ft every 30 days, so the pair uses 30 days on all three tracks).

Chinch bugs: always count before treating. Push a bottomless can 3 in into the soil at 4 spots on the edge of the damage, fill with water, count for 5 minutes, and write the count in the visit notes. Big-eyed bugs (wide head, bulging eyes) are predators: do not count them. Recheck a treated area at 5 and 12 days. Where chinch bugs are found at the edge of a damaged patch (4 gal per 1,000 sq ft into the thatch): Tetrino in May, then Arena, then bifenthrin, then Dylox 6.2 G. Arena: 0.147 oz per 1,000 sq ft (6.4 oz per acre, the low end of the label's turf range; about 1.4 level teaspoons), up to 2 applications per lawn per year at least 8 weeks (56 days) apart (app-enforced). Two applications reach the label's yearly limit of 12.8 oz per acre (0.4 lb clothianidin per acre); after that, use bifenthrin, which is not a neonicotinoid. On St. Augustine this rate and the 8-week repeat are Valent's Florida 2(ee) recommendation for southern chinch bug (EPA Reg. No. 59639-152; expires December 31, 2028): keep a copy on the truck. Keep Arena off blooming plants where bees forage, and keep children and pets off until the spray has dried.

Sugarcane mosaic virus (lethal viral necrosis) is confirmed in Sarasota, Manatee and Charlotte. Yellow streaks between the veins on Floratam or ProVista, in any month (most often September to January), with no chinch bugs: photo, note and call the office; Waves sends live streaked leaves with their roots to the UF Plant Diagnostic Center at its own cost (roots too, because take-all can come with the virus). Do not sell a fungicide or insecticide for it (UF: pesticides do not work). Mow or walk suspect lawns last. For new sod, recommend Palmetto or CitraBlue, never Floratam or ProVista.
Caterpillars: Acelepryn, then bifenthrin, with a 7-day recheck. Acelepryn on caterpillars: delay watering (irrigation) or mowing for 24 hours after application.
Bifenthrin: delay watering 24 hours on every use. Grubs and mole crickets: Dylox 6.2 G on spreader visits only, watered in.

Mole cricket nymphs, June and the July scout visit (UF/IFAS and Clemson: treat small nymphs from mid-June through July, before they grow): Advion Insect Granule (indoxacarb, Group 22A) on the tunnel areas, 3 lb per 1,000 sq ft of treated area by hand shaker. It is a bait and a spot tool, not a whole-lawn tool, so the one-tool rule holds. If the soil is dry, water the spot lightly BEFORE applying. Apply late in the day to dry grass. Then no irrigation and no rain-dependent watering for 3 days. On the June hose visit, the bait goes on after the micronutrient pass has dried. Label yearly maximum: 4.6 lb per 1,000 sq ft, so Advion goes on a spot once a year, at 3 lb. The July visit is for new tunnel areas that were not baited in June. Fall adults and bigger mole crickets go to Dylox 6.2 G. Acelepryn is not a mole cricket product in this program.

Weeds: Celsius plus Certainty (0.085 oz plus 0.028 oz per 1,000 sq ft, NIS 0.25%); once the Celsius annual cap is reached, Blindside Herbicide in its place from November through March (April through October: no weed spray once the Celsius cap is reached). In February the weed spot is Celsius alone: no Certainty and no surfactant. Blindside goes on at 0.149 oz per 1,000 sq ft, one application per lawn per year (label: the warm-season rate is 0.149 to 0.23 oz a pass, and no more than 0.23 oz per 1,000 sq ft (10 oz per acre) a year). Dismiss: use up the jug on green kyllinga under 85°F, no rain or irrigation for 24 hours after (owner 2026-10-09: every post-emergent herbicide holds 24 hours); do not reorder.
Dry spots: Dispatch Sprayable.

Other spot diseases (secondary lines): Pythium root rot with Artavia in June, July and August (September's Artavia is the take-all pass only, so a take-all application stays unambiguous); fairy ring with Velista and a wetting agent; dollar spot on bermuda and zoysia with Velista or Gravex, never Artavia (its label says it does not control dollar spot); rust on zoysia with Velista or Gravex; leaf spot or melting out on bermuda with Velista. The app warns on the second Artavia application for Pythium; the label allows two in a row. Headway is not a rotation for it (Headway has the same Group 11 ingredient). Do not make a third Group 11 application in a row: fix the watering or drainage.

Fire ant granule (Topchoice Granular Insecticide) is an optional add-on in April or October, both spreader visits, one application per lawn per year. The office prices it. It is not part of the base visit.
Ronstar / oxadiazon: never on residential home lawns (label: not for use on home lawns); commercial turf per label.

Soil tests: triggers only (owner 2026-10-31). Take a sample only when one of these is true: a new sod or new-build lawn is not thriving 60 days after install; yellowing stays after the iron spot test, or the lawn is no better after 2 visits with no pest or disease found (October to May only); it is a bahia or pasture-origin lawn; or phosphorus is planned in Manatee County. One sample per lawn, once (two only when a problem spot differs from the rest of the lawn); never retest. Pull 10 to 15 cores from the top 4 in, mix them, and bag 1 pint; never mix healthy and problem turf, and never sample right after a fertilizer or lime pass. The office mails it to the UF/IFAS Extension Soil Testing Laboratory (standard test, form SL136) and records the test date and pH in the turf profile. Act on three results only: lime at the report's lime rate; magnesium (Epsom salt, rate set by the office) when Mg is below 20 ppm; phosphorus only when P is 20 mg/kg or lower (Mehlich-3) and the report is filed with Manatee County. Any other result changes nothing. A soil test comes before a UF plant lab sample, never both at once. Lab reports are not sent to customers unless the owner says so.

Plant-parasitic nematodes: when a lawn keeps thinning, with short, stubby roots and no chinch bugs, and its soil test (above) found nothing to act on, the office sends one soil-and-root sample to the UF/IFAS Nematode Assay Lab at Waves' own cost, taken the way the lab's turf form says. One sample per lawn, once. Nothing is sold for nematodes (UF/IFAS: home lawns have no reliable nematode control). Lab reports are not sent to customers unless the owner says so.

Fertilizer safety: deflector shield on the spreader, a 10 ft fertilizer-free band from any water body, wetland, seawall or top of bank, no fertilizing when a severe thunderstorm, flood or tropical watch or warning is forecast, sweep fertilizer off driveways, sidewalks and streets back onto the lawn, Manatee BMP decal on the vehicle.

North Port: no Nutra-TECH on the June, August and September visits until the city confirms. The April Nutra-TECH pass stays. The plan holds the summer product back and a completion that records it is flagged.

Season 2027 (visits from 2027-10-01), 12-visit plan only. This is a note and changes no 2026 visit: October LESCO 24-0-11 with PolyPlus OPTI at 2.5 lb per 1,000 sq ft (0.60 lb N); November LESCO Dimension 0.21% 18-0-10 at 4.04 lb per 1,000 sq ft (0.73 lb N, 0.37 lb dithiopyr per acre, the commercial label Coastal South rate). January Stonewall 4FL stays. December is defined separately. The 9-visit plan keeps the October Dimension step.
